rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author describes God's decree concerning the fighting as wise.
rows.anchor: حكيما فيما قضى من ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view says God knows both sides and is wise in what He commands concerning them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عليم بكم وبهم، حكيم فيما أمركم فيهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view stresses God's wisdom in what He decreed about the matter.
rows.anchor: حكيما فيما قضى من ذلك، وقيل: عليم بكم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Obeying the command of the Wise is obligatory.
rows.anchor: واتباع أمر الحكيم واجب، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fighting is obligatory even when it causes pain, because its consequences are hoped to bring benefit.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على وجوب الجهاد وإن أصابته الآلام لما يرجى من عواقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires strengthening oneself as much as possible.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب تقوية النفس ما أمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It requires initiating jihad, since the command to pursue them came without a prior cause.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب الجهاد ابتداء؛ لأنه أوجب طلبهم من غير تقدم سبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An obligation cannot be abandoned merely from fear of hardship.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الواجب لا يسع تركه لخوف المكاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fighter may fight in pursuit of reward.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن للمجاهد أن يجاهد لطلب الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fighter may seek assistance.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه يجوز له طلب المعونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Debate and counterargument are valid; the statement that opponents suffer as Muslims do is a counterargument.
rows.anchor: وتدل على جواز الحجاج وصحة المعارضة؛ لأن قوله: فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون معارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is putting a thing in its proper place as wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: الحق: وضع الشيء موضعه على ما تقضيه الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an attribute of God, al-Haqq means the possessor of right; for the Book it can mean possessing truth or being set according to wisdom.
rows.anchor: ويقال لله تعالى الحق، أي ذو الحق، وفي الكتاب أنه حق معنيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مخاصمة means dispute; خصم works for singular or plural and for masculine or feminine, while خصام is the verbal noun of خاصم.
rows.anchor: والمخاصمة: المنازعة، والخصم يستوي فيه الواحد والجمع والذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traitor is the opposite of a trustworthy person; the root sense of betrayal is deficiency or taking away.
rows.anchor: والخائن: ضد الأمين، وأصله الخيانة، وأصله النقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ب can attach to أنزل, meaning God sent the Book down in truth; another parsing says it descended upon truth and made truth clear.
rows.anchor: الباء في قوله: بالحق يعني أنزل. على وجه الحق، وقيل: نزل على الحق

rows.speaker: السدي والضحاك
rows.claim: They say the verse concerned Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq, who denied keeping a deposited coat of mail; his relatives defended him without proof, and the Prophet nearly sided with them before revelation exposed the case.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية في درع كانت وديعة

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say Tuʿma stole a coat of mail and his relatives argued on his behalf.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه سرق درعا فجادل عنه قومه عن الحسن وابن زيد

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada recounts how Banu Ubayriq stole food and weapons from Rifaʿa ibn Zayd, blamed the righteous Muslim Lubayd, and accused Qatada when he reported them; revelation identified the traitors, and Bishr later fled to the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة بن النعمان قال: كان أهل بيت منا يقال لهم بنو أبيرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الهم is what one intends or thinks to do; الهمة likewise denotes aspiration, and الهمام is a king of great aspiration.
rows.anchor: الهم: ما هممت، وكذلك الهمة. والهمام: الملك العظيم الهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of misguidance is destruction by turning away from the path of salvation toward ruin.
rows.anchor: والإضلال: أصله الإهلاك بالعدول عن طريق النجاة إلى طريق الهلاك

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn ʿIsa says najwa means secret conversation, as the other linguists Ibn Durayd and al-Khalil also hold.
rows.anchor: النجوى قال علي بن عيسى: هو الإسرار عند سائر أهل اللغة، منهم ابن دريد والخليل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says najwa can mean what two or more people share privately or openly; Ali ibn ʿIsa rejects this as mistaken.
rows.anchor: وزعم الزجاج أن معنى النجوى ما ينفرد به الجماعة أو الاثنان سرا كان أو ظاهرا، وهو غلط منه

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: The word najwa derives from elevation: a secret is raised by revealing it to another, just as skin is lifted when peeled.
rows.anchor: وأصل النجوة: الارتفاع، فسمي الإسرار نجوى؛ لأنه رفع السر عنك بإظهاره لغيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related word النجا means speed because it involves rising; ʿAli's phrase النجاء النجاء calls for hastening to obedience.
rows.anchor: والنجا: السرعة؛ لأنه ارتفاع فيه، ومنه: النجاء النجاء في كلام أمير المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes من genitive by following كثير: there is no good in many of their private talks except among those who command charity; نجوى then means the people conferring.
rows.anchor: موضعها جر على الإتباع ل (الكثير)، يعني: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا فيمن أمر بصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis makes من accusative as a disconnected exception, meaning that the person who commands charity or good has something good.
rows.anchor: أن تكون نصبا على الاستثناء المنقطع، كأنه قيل: ليكن من أمر بصدقة أو كذا ففيه خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes من nominative by extension, treating the person who commands charity as the good private conversation, like the cited verse about gazelles and camels being a place's only company.
rows.anchor: أدت تكون رفعا على قول الشاعر: وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Genitive is also possible by construing the phrase as نجوى من أمر بصدقة; the author prefers this connected reading over a disconnected exception when meaning permits.
rows.anchor: والجر أولى؛ لأن حمل الكلام على الاتصال أولى من الانقطاع، إذا لم يخل بالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attempted misguidance turns no one from truth except themselves; alternatively, they destroy only themselves, so its punishment returns on them while the Prophet is unharmed.
rows.anchor: وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم أي ما يزيلون عن الحق إلا أنفسهم، وقيل: وما يهلكون إلا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet through testimony: God guides him and exposes their intentions so he will not grant their request.
rows.anchor: قيل: لا يضرونك بشهادة؛ لأن الله تعالى يسددك في أمورك، ويبين لك ما أضمروا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view identifies them as the Thaqif delegation, whose request could not harm the Prophet because God's care kept him from accepting it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم وفد ثقيف لم يضروه بما التمسوا؛ لأنه ثبت بلطف الله فلم يجبهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they were hypocrites who intended to assassinate the Prophet, but God protected him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم المنافقون هموا بالفتك به فدفع الله عنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view identifies them as unbelievers who cannot harm the Prophet's religion or erase his prophethood because God supports him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم الكافرون لا يضرونك في دينك وإزالة نبوتك؛ لأنه تعالى يؤيدك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Here the Book is the Qur'an and wisdom is the rulings contained in it.
rows.anchor: قيل: الكتاب: القرآن، والحكمة: ما فيه من الأحكام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies wisdom as the Sunna.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الحكمة: السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their effort to mislead is implausible when God is revealing the Book and teaching the Prophet its rulings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كيف يضلونك، وهو ينزل عليك الكتاب ويوحي إليك بالأحكام؟!

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: What God taught the Prophet includes the laws and religious ordinances.
rows.anchor: وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم قيل: من الشرائع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God taught him reports about earlier and later peoples and what has been and will be.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من أخبار الأولين والآخرين وما كان وما يكون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says God's favor was great from the Prophet's creation until his mission.
rows.anchor: قيل: فضله عليك - منذ خلقك إلى أن بعثك - عظيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view locates its greatness in making him the seal of prophets and master of messengers and giving him intercession and other gifts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عظيم حيث جعلك خاتم النبيين وسيد المرسلين، وأعطاك الشفاعة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نجواهم means their secret conversations.
rows.anchor: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم أي إسرارهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrase may refer generally to people's private conversations.
rows.anchor: قيل: نجوى الناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the talkers as Tuʿma's relatives, who defended the traitor.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذين ذبوا عن الخائن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as hypocrites who secretly planned what God disapproved.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم المنافقون الذين حكى الله عنهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as the Thaqif delegation.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم وفد ثقيف

words: إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف
rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the good is in one who commands what is right, rather than in the hidden conversation kept from the Prophet and Muslims.
rows.anchor: لكن الخير فيمن يأمر بالمعروف عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To command charity means to urge people to give it.
rows.anchor: إلا من أمر بصدقة يعني حث عليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Maʿruf means commanding what is right, the various forms of piety that sound minds recognize.
rows.anchor: قيل: أمر بمعروف، وهو أبواب البر، سمي معروفا لاعتراف العقول بها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says it is called maʿruf because people of goodness recognize its practitioners.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأن أهل الخير يعرفونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reconciliation between people means bringing them together in affection.
rows.anchor: أو إصلاح بين الناس قيل: يؤلفون بين الناس بالمحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's pleasure means seeking His approval.
rows.anchor: ابتغاء مرضاة الله أي طلب رضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great reward is recompense and abundant merit: it lasts, comes with honor, and is free of anything that could spoil it.
rows.anchor: أجرا أي عوضا ومثوبة عظيمة في الكثرة والمنزلة والصفة، أما الكثرة فلأنه دائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not heed a prayer against His Messenger, especially a request that would obstruct what He commanded; a prophet cannot ask for faith to be removed, and God cannot strip faith from someone and then punish him for it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز على نبي الله أن يدعو بسلب الإيمان، ولا يجوز على الله تعالى أن يسلب إيمان أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilāwa means recitation, but its root sense is following: one may say تلوت الرجل تلوا, I followed the man.
rows.anchor: التلاوة: تلوت القرآن تلاوة، وتلوت الرجل تلوا: تبعته، وهو الأصل في الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qurban is an offering used to draw near to God; a king's qurabān are visitors seeking nearness to him, and the word is on the pattern فعْلان from قرب.
rows.anchor: والقربان: ما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى، وقربان الملك وقرابينه: زواره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root first denotes nearness in place and then extends to nearness in rank; قربان follows the pattern of عدوان, فرقان, سكران, and كفران.
rows.anchor: والقربان وزنه فعلان، من القرب، كالعدوان من العدو، والفرقان من الفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bast is extension, the opposite of contraction, as spreading is opposite to folding.
rows.anchor: والبسط: المد المنافي للقبض، وهما نقيضان كالنشر والطي

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn ʿIsa connects the story to Jewish injustice and broken covenants, rebuking them, warning that wrongdoing returns on its perpetrators, and consoling the Prophet for their treatment.
rows.anchor: إن حال اليهود في الظلم ونقض العهد، كحال ابن آدم في ظلمه لأخيه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim connects the story to the command to debate the People of the Book from scripture and disclose its hidden reports as proof of the Prophet's truthfulness.
rows.anchor: عن أسرار ما في كتابهم، شاهدا على صدقه، وهذا من أسرار أحاديثهم عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The story follows the command to tell them about Adam's sons so they can learn that obedience, disobedience, and their consequences follow the same pattern.
rows.anchor: اذكر لهم حديث ابني آدم ليعلموا أن سبيلهم في الطاعة والمعصية وعاقبتها كسبيلهم

rows.speaker: أبو حامد
rows.claim: Abu Hamid links the story to the People of the Book claiming to be God's children and beloved: descent from prophets does not save unbelievers, as Adam's son shows.
rows.anchor: يتصل بقوله: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه أي: لا ينفعهم كونهم من أولاد الأنبياء مع كفرهم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says the People of the Book rejected Muhammad out of envy, so the story warns them that envy leads to a bad end.
rows.anchor: أخبرهم بخبر ابن آدم، وما ناله من الحسد من سوء العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بوء means return; the phrase وباءوا بغضب الله says they returned with God's anger, while بواء describes people who return to the same standing.
rows.anchor: البوء: الرجوع، ومنه: (وباءوا بغضب من الله) أي: رجعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طاع means to come willingly, انطاع to yield, and أطاع to carry out a command; طاوع means to agree with someone.
rows.anchor: ويقال: طاع لفلان كذا: إذا أتاه طوعا، وانطاع: انقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase هو طوعة, cited in al-ʿAyn, the person follows or yields to another.
rows.anchor: وفي العين: هو طوعة: إذا انقاد معه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: They take my sin as the sin of killing me and your sin as the sin you committed before the killing, which caused your offering to be rejected.
rows.anchor: إثم قتلي وإثمك الذي كان منك قبل قتلي، عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك

rows.speaker: أبو علي والزجاج
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli and al-Zajjaj take your sin to mean the offense that caused your offering not to be accepted.
rows.anchor: إثمك الذي من أجله لم يتقبل قربانك، عن أبي علي والزجاج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes my sin as the murder and your sin as the killing of all people, since the first murderer established the practice.
rows.anchor: إثمي: إثم قتلي، وإثمك هو قتل جميع الناس حيث سن القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To return carrying my sin means to bear its punishment: no one may desire disobedience to God, but one may desire the punishment that is deserved, as one may wish unbelievers their punishment.
rows.anchor: ومعنى تبوء بإثمي، أي: بعقاب إثمي؛ لأنه لا يجوز لأحد أن يريد معصية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means those who remain with the Fire; the consequence is the punishment of the Fire, the recompense of wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فتكون من أصحاب النار الملازمين للنار وذلك يعني عذاب النار جزاء الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that his own soul helped him carry out the murder.
rows.anchor: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه قيل: ساعدته نفسه على قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says his soul emboldened him to kill his brother.
rows.anchor: شجعته، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says his soul made the murder seem attractive to him.
rows.anchor: زينت له نفسه قتل أخيه، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأبو مالك
rows.claim: They say Cain killed his brother while he slept by smashing his head with a rock.
rows.anchor: قتل أخاه، وهو نائم، شدخ رأسه بصخرة، عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأبي مالك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Cain did not know how to kill; Satan demonstrated by smashing a bird's head, and Cain learned from him.
rows.anchor: لم يدر كيف يقتله فظهر له إبليس وأخذ طيرا، وشدخ رأسه، فقتله، فتعلم منه، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view says this was the first killing among humanity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه أول قتيل في الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hizb is a party or group; its root sense is an affliction that befalls someone, and people with common hearts and deeds form a party even without meeting.
rows.anchor: الحزب: الطائفة، والجماعة، والأحزاب الجمع، وأصله النائبة، من قولهم: حزبه الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of parties echoes the verse that communities split into factions, each rejoicing in what it has.
rows.anchor: فتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم زبرا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون (53)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawla here is the one who undertakes to support the person allied with him.
rows.anchor: والمولى: المتولي لنصر من يتولاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is the subject and the following clause its predicate, with an implied result: whoever allies with God is victorious.
rows.anchor: (من) في قوله: ومن يتول الله ورسوله مبتدأ، والجملة بعده خبر

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: When ʿUbada ibn al-Samit broke with the Jews and allied with God and His Messenger, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy opposed him; this occasion is attributed to ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية في عبادة بن الصامت لما تبرأ من اليهود، وتولى الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another occasion was the Prophet's decision to fight Banu Qaynuqa, allies of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy; Saʿd and ʿUbada ibn al-Samit disavowed them while ʿAbd Allah opposed the decision.
rows.anchor: قتل بني قينقاع، وكانوا حلفاء عبد الله بن أبي، وسعد بن عبادة وعبادة بن الصامت

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: When the Jews shunned the newly converted ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, he complained to the Prophet, then declared himself content with God, His Messenger, and the believers as allies.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما أسلم عبد الله بن سلام هجره اليهود من موالاته وكلامه ومجالسته

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say the verse was revealed when ʿAli gave his ring as charity while bowing.
rows.anchor: تصدق بخاتمه وهو راكع، عن مجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: A similar long report from Abu Dharr says a beggar received ʿAli's ring while ʿAli was bowing and gestured with his ring-bearing right pinkie; the author says God knows whether the report is sound, and it quotes Moses' prayer.
rows.anchor: وروي نحوه عن أبي ذر في حديث طويل - الله أعلم بصحته - أن سائلا سأل في المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verse shows that no injustice exceeds this offense, which establishes its unbelief; associating God with creatures, accusing Him of unjust judgment, or attributing evil acts to Him is also unbelief.
rows.anchor: وتدل على كفر من شبه الله بخلقه، أو جوره في حكمه، وأضاف إليه قبيحا في أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that the Qur'an has not been matched; anyone claiming to have matched it is lying.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن القرآن لم يعارض، وأن كل من ادعى مثل ذلك فهو كاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those guilty of this offense receive the greatest punishment, since lying against God is the greatest sin.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن أعظم العقاب عقاب هؤلاء، وهذا لا شبهة فيه؛ لأنه إذا كان أعظم الذنوب الكذب على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage urges reflection on God's signs and warns that arrogance toward them is a grave sin.
rows.anchor: وتدل على وجوب التفكر في الآيات وعظم ذنب من استكبر عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People see the angels at death because God strengthens their sight so that they see them while others do not.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه يعاين الملائكة في حال النزع، وذلك إنما يكون بأن يقوي الله شعاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Nafiʿ, Hafs from ʿAsim, and al-Kisaʾi read بينكم in the accusative; Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Masʿud, and Abu Musa also transmit this reading, while the other readers use the nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي: بينكم نصبا، وهو قراءة الحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative بين, the meaning is that the ties you maintained in worldly life are severed; بين can mean either connection or separation, and here it is a noun, not an adverb.
rows.anchor: فأما الرفع فعلى معنى تقطع وصلكم الذي كنتم تواصلون بها في الدنيا، والبين: الوصل، والبين: القطيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative بين, an implied ما gives the sense 'what was between you was severed'; the phrase refers to the partnership and بين is an adverb.
rows.anchor: على إضمار (ما)، أي: تقطع ما بينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فرادى means individually or alone; it is pluralized from فريد or فرد, like أسير/أسارى and وحد/آحاد, as al-Farra notes.
rows.anchor: الفرادى: الوحدان، وهم المنفردون، واحده: فريد، وفعيل يجمع على فعالى كأسير وأسارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To give someone خول is to make him an owner of dependents, like giving him wealth or authority; خوله الله means He granted him something, and خولي مال means a steward of property.
rows.anchor: والتخويل: تمليك الخول، كما أن التمويل تمليك الأموال. والتسويد تمليك السؤدد، وخوله الله: أعطاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the Prophet would يتخول people with admonition, meaning he attended to them regularly; Abu ʿAmr corrects this to يتحولهم, choosing times when they were receptive.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: كان يتخولهم بالموعظة أي: يتعهدهم، وقال أبو عمرو: الصواب يتحولهم بالحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase خول so-and-so can mean his followers; خائل is singular, and a gift given without recompense is also described as granting خول.
rows.anchor: ويقال: هم خول فلان أي: أتباعه، الواحد: خائل، وكل من أعطى عطاء على غير جزاء فقد خوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questioning, weighing, reckoning, and testimony would have no purpose if God could punish people without first establishing their case.
rows.anchor: يعاقب ابتداء لم يكن في ذلك فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers generally pronounce معايش without hamza; Kharija's report from Nafiʿ and al-Aʿraj use hamza, but Mujahid calls the attribution to Nafiʿ erroneous.
rows.anchor: أجمع القراء على معايش بغير همز إلا ما روى خارجة عن نافع أنه همزها، وعن الأعرج أيضا بالهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza is considered incorrect because the word's medial y is a root letter; hamza is appropriate in faʿāʾil forms with added y or w, though analogy with those forms makes the variant weakly defensible.
rows.anchor: إن الهمز فيه لحن؛ لأن الياء فيها عين الفعل أصلية، ولم تعرض فيها علة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamkin is granting the means to act while removing impediments; Ibn ʿArafa defines it as the disappearance of obstacles.
rows.anchor: التمكين: إعطاء ما يصح به الفعل مع رفع المانع، قال ابن عرفة: التمكين زوال الموانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معايش is the plural of livelihood: life and what sustains it, including crops, livestock, and similar provisions.
rows.anchor: والمعايش: جمعم عيشة، وأصله من العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation means bringing something into existence according to its measure; another definition is producing it without a prior model.
rows.anchor: والخلق: إحداث الشيء على تقديره، وأصله التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taswir is giving something a form; a sura is a structure with a visible shape.
rows.anchor: والتصوير: جعل الشيء على صورة، والصورة بنية على هيئة ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration originally means lowering oneself; in religious law it means putting the forehead on the ground, as the cited poetry describes hillocks as prostrate under hooves.
rows.anchor: والسجود: أصله الانخفاض، وهو في الشرع: وضع الجبهة على الأرض قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes قليلا accusative under يشكرون and treats ما as an added particle; another takes the sense as neither a little nor much gratitude, and a third as 'your gratitude is little.'
rows.anchor: قليلا: نصب بوقوع (يشكرون) عليه، و(ما) صلة، وقيل تقديره: ما يشكرون قليلا ولا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls the gifts of land and its provisions alongside the gifts of revealed books and messengers, then recalls God's gifts to Adam, humanity's father.
rows.anchor: تذكير للنعم بالتمكين في الأرض، وما خلق فيها من الأرزاق مضافا إلى نعمه بإنزال الكتب وإرسال الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although creation and forming are mentioned after land-enablement, they happened earlier; the sense is that God created and formed people, settled them on earth, and provided good things and livelihoods.
rows.anchor: وتقديره: خلقكم وصوركم، ومكنكم في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' prostration demonstrates Adam's great rank and a distinction for his descendants; the Zaydi shaykhs infer that the Prophet's descendants likewise have virtue by descent.
rows.anchor: وتدل على عظيم رتبة آدم إذ أسجد له ملائكته، ورتبة لأولاده بكونهم من ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis too had been commanded to prostrate, and the angels' compliance is praised while his refusal is blamed.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن إبليس كان مأمورا بالسجود، وتدل على أن السجود فعلهم لذلك مدح على فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three analyses are offered: لا is an emphatic extra particle, the phrase means 'what prompted you not to prostrate,' or it means 'what impelled you to refuse'; al-Farra sees reinforcement after the preceding negation, and another parses it as 'who told you not to prostrate?'.
rows.anchor: قوله: ما منعك ألا تسجد فيه ثلاثة أقوال: الأول: أن تكون (لا) صلة مؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is nominative as 'what thing prevented you'; أن is accusative as the object of منع.
rows.anchor: رفع على تقدير: أي شيء منعك من السجود، و(أن) في موضع نصب بوقوع المنع عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in فما يكون لك is nominative in the parsing of the clause about arrogance.
rows.anchor: و(ما) في قوله: عما يكون في موضع رفع أي: فما يكون لك التكبر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هبوط is descent toward a lower place; the word is also used when an illness abates.
rows.anchor: الهبوط: الانحدار إلى جهة السفل، ومنه: هبط المرض لحم العليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takabbur is displaying one's greatness, which is blameworthy in a servant.
rows.anchor: والتكبر: إظهار كبره، فهو ذم في صفة العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A صاغر is humiliated and low in rank; the root is صغر, and the self may become diminished through disgrace.
rows.anchor: والصاغر: الذليل لصغر القدر، صغر صغرا وصغارا، وتصاغرت إليه نفسه ذلا ومهانة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says the statement was spoken by one of the angels on God's behalf.
rows.anchor: قاله على لسان بعض ملائكته، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God Himself spoke the words, as the miracle indicates.
rows.anchor: وقيل: [بل قاله الله]- تعالى -[ودل المعجز] أنه كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what turned Iblis away, not what literally prevented him, since he was not barred from obeying an order; a diversion is like prevention, just as a summons is like compulsion.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد المنع؛ لأنه لم يكن ممنوعا من السجود إذ لو كان ممنوعا لما أمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis argues that fire is superior to clay, therefore he is better than Adam and will not prostrate to him.
rows.anchor: فلما كان النار خيرا من الطين كنت خيرا من آدم، فلا أسجد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's hostility toward Adam's children manifests in his eagerness to misguide them.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الضلال فعل إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also shows that most human beings are ungrateful and that misguidance is Satan's act.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن أكثر بني آدم غير شاكرين. وتدل على أن الضلال فعل إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has malikayn with fatḥa on the lām; Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak read malikayn with kasra, linking it to the promise of an unfading kingdom in 20:120.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: ملكين بفتح اللام، وعن ابن عباس والضحاك ملكين بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذأم and ذيم mean severe blame, with or without hamza; the text gives their verb forms and related form ذمه.
rows.anchor: الذأم والذيم: أشد العيب بالهمز وترك الهمز، ويقال: ذأمه يذأمه ذأما

rows.speaker: ابن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmr says ذأمته means he humiliated and cast someone away; ذام and زجر likewise denote expulsion or driving off in disgrace.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمرو: ذأمته: إذا حقرته وأبعدته، والذام: الطرد والإبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is a quiet prompting toward something, like a faint rustling sound; the verse from Ruʾba uses the word for whispering in prayer.
rows.anchor: والوسوسة: الدعاء إلى أمر بصوت خفي كالخشخشة، وسوس يوسوس وسوسة، قال رؤبة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim defines waswas as excessive, disordered speech, which explains why a confused person is called mawsoos.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: الوسواس الإكثار من الكلام على غير نظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إبداء is making something appear; بدو means appearance, and the phrase بدا له الرأي describes a change in one's judgment.
rows.anchor: والإبداء: اني ظهار، والبدو الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muwārāt and concealment are equivalent: a thing is placed behind a covering, as when a dead person is hidden in earth; the wording in 5:31 illustrates this sense.
rows.anchor: والمواراة والستر واحد في المعنى وأصله جعل الشيء وراء ما ستره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawʾa means the genitals because their exposure is disliked; anything shameful to reveal can also be called sawʾa.
rows.anchor: والسوءة: الفرج؛ لأنه يسوء صاحبه إظهاره، وكل ما قبح إظهاره فهو سوأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasam, yamin, and half are synonyms for an oath; the reciprocal form evokes an exchange of oaths, while the root suggests dividing the proof between parties, as in تقاسموا meaning they swore together.
rows.anchor: والقسم واليمين والحلف نظائر، وإنما ذكر على المفاعلة؛ لأنه في معنى المقابلة
